clue.text: Dominate on show

blocks.note: over in the sense of on top of
to bear is to show or display, as a sign bears a name

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of an exhibition or performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On show' reads as one phrase but splits into two short synonyms placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbear is to overwhelm or domineer, pressing down on others by force or authority.

clue.text: An examination in morality

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters sit inside the following word

blocks.note: the run of letters after the first M

explanation.surface: A test of someone's ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken exam, as in a viva or language test.

clue.text: Formerly caught basking in shade, like the dodo?

indicators.note: something basking lies inside the warmth around it, so one piece sits within the next

blocks.note: ex- means former
a tint is a shade of colour
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A sunbathing animal was once captured, perhaps like a famously lost bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basking in shade' reads as lounging in the cool; it means the catch letter sits inside the colour word. The question mark flags the dodo as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is the classic example of a species that died out, so extinct describes it.

clue.text: Hood in Virginia following a cab, all agitated

indicators.note: agitated letters are shaken up and land in a new order
following puts the state abbreviation after the other part

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A hoodlum in Virginia chases a taxi in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' suggests a gangster in the surface, but here it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A balaclava is a close-fitting woollen hood covering head and neck, leaving the face partly open.

clue.text: Suitable nick

blocks.note: first meaning: fitting, proper
second meaning: to steal, take for oneself

explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for steal; the adjective and the verb are spelt alike but said differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for fitting and a verb for taking something without permission.

clue.text: Pen note about one in block

indicators.note: about means going around, so the note surrounds the number

blocks.note: a pig's pen is a sty
me is a variant spelling of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Writing a short message about someone in an apartment building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' and 'note' look like writing; one is a pig enclosure, the other a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie someone is to obstruct or thwart them, a sense from a golf ball blocking the hole.

clue.text: Fish off Turkey, seawards

blocks.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
out to sea, away from shore

explanation.surface: Fishing in the waters off the Turkish coast, heading out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Swallow one gin and vermouth

blocks.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to down a single cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail mixed from gin and dry vermouth.

clue.text: In Greece, men's deceptive appearances

indicators.note: something deceptive is not what it seems, so these letters hide another word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Greek men are said to look different from how they really are.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergence is a coming into view, so emergences are appearances or arrivals.

clue.text: This animal could make worker run away

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker
to elope is to run away to marry

explanation.surface: Some creature is frightening enough to send a labourer fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The antelope is a swift, horned grazing mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Reportedly vulgar passage

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the spoken form of a word counts here

blocks.note: coarse means vulgar, and is said the same as its partner

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be crude in the way they pass by.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a passage or route, as of a river or of time.

clue.text: Prepared to risk everything, so no other joint will do

definitions.text: so no other joint will do

blocks.note: first meaning: staking all on one attempt

blocks.clueFragment: so no other joint will do
blocks.note: second meaning, read cryptically: a diner who will take the neck cut of meat or go without

explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the phrase literally: a joint is a cut of meat, and the customer accepts only one cut or none.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes going all out, accepting total success or total failure.

clue.text: Assumed name of rogue mender, criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent out of its proper shape

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy repairman operates under an alias.
explanation.definitionFit: A nom de guerre, French for war name, is a pseudonym adopted for a cause or campaign.

clue.text: Evil crime involved importing Latin pasta

indicators.note: importing means bringing something in, so a letter is added inside
involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are twisted together

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A wicked offence involved smuggling Italian food.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermicelli is a very thin variety of pasta, its name meaning little worms.

clue.text: Not included in special edition

blocks.note: first meaning: charged on top
second meaning: a special issue of a newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a limited release; 'in' just joins two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional charge left out of the basic price, and also a newspaper's special issue.

clue.text: Touching, calling for forgiveness

blocks.note: re means concerning or touching on
a calling or vocation is one's mission

explanation.surface: A moving plea asking to be pardoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' and 'calling' look like emotion and shouting; they mean about and vocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission of sins is their pardon, so remission can mean forgiveness.

clue.text: Speaks about a son and daughter making a musical

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word wraps the family members

blocks.note: says is a synonym of speaks
taken as written
a son is a lad
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent talks about their children putting on a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The family members go inside the speaking word, just after its first letter. Calling a son a lad is loose but common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad Days is a 1954 British stage musical by Julian Slade, one of the longest-running of its era.

clue.text: Spoil old lady and boy with English jam

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil
one's old lady is mother, ma
a lad is a boy
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Indulging an elderly woman and a child with a sweet English preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' suggests pampering in the surface; it means damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a preserve made from citrus fruit, a kind of jam.

clue.text: Fox pelt said to be on a road?

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for the weather counts by its sound

blocks.note: to pelt is to rain hard; the spoken word supplies the opening sound
taken as written
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A fox's skin is apparently lying on a road, roadkill perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like the fox's fur; it is the verb for heavy rain. 'To be on' puts the sound before A RD.
explanation.definitionFit: Reynard is the traditional name for the fox in medieval fable.

clue.text: Slip in left part of church

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: Someone trips in the left-hand section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or small error, as in a lapse of memory.

clue.text: Trellis made from a bulky piece of wood agent erected

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a log is a thick piece of wood
rep, short for representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: A garden frame built from a heavy timber that someone put up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is an arbour or trellis framework over a walk, for climbing plants.

clue.text: Make an unwarranted fuss, and duly rub mercer the wrong way

indicators.note: rubbing the wrong way disturbs the natural order, so letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Complaining loudly about irritating a cloth merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: A mercer is a dealer in fine fabrics; 'rub the wrong way' is an idiom for annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry blue murder is to protest loudly and excessively, an idiom for overreacting.

clue.text: Divulge information got from head of language college

indicators.note: head of a word means its opening letter only

blocks.note: the opening letter of language
Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

explanation.surface: A source within a language school leaked details.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is the idiom for revealing a secret or telling what one knows.

clue.text: A flighty creature up to some criminal activity

blocks.note: taken as written
a tit is a small bird, a creature of flight

explanation.surface: A fickle person is engaged in wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests capricious in the surface; here it means able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at it again is up to their usual tricks or mischief, an idiom.

clue.text: Slowly locking a shed

indicators.note: locking means shutting something in, so one part holds the other inside

blocks.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes their time securing an outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, its roof leaning on it.

clue.text: Appear suddenly, blooming after holiday

indicators.note: after places the flowering word behind the other one

blocks.note: a break is a short holiday
flowers that are out are in bloom

explanation.surface: Flowers spring up after a vacation away.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash or fighting can break out, arising suddenly and spreading.

clue.text: I eat after one - duck?

indicators.note: after puts the verb behind the two single letters

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they get to eat after a bird has gone first.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'I' looks like the speaker but is the definition: I is iodine's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the chemical symbol of iodine, a halogen element.

clue.text: Bird studied, we hear, at dawn

indicators.note: we hear means heard rather than seen, so the sound of the past tense counts

blocks.note: read, past tense, means studied and sounds like the colour
the dawn of something is its start

explanation.surface: A bird observed at first light, by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail, 'start' being an old word for tail.
